draft.assessment: PTSD is active with chronic pain comorbidity; current care includes sertraline. The evidence base provides veteran-focused pain education and mechanistic links between PTSD and cardiovascular risk, but none offers direct PTSD-specific pharmacologic or psychotherapeutic guidance for this patient.

recommended_plan.text: Provide pain neuroscience education to reduce pain distress and improve PTSD-related functioning.
recommended_plan.rationale: LOCAL-02908 shows pain neuroscience education improves PTSD, disability, and pain self-efficacy in veterans.
cautions: Evidence limited to veterans; generalizability may vary.

recommended_plan.text: Perform cardiovascular risk assessment and integrate standard CVD risk management.
recommended_plan.rationale: LOCAL-02091 documents brain-heart axis involvement linking PTSD and CVD.
cautions: Mechanistic association; not a direct PTSD treatment.

monitoring: Monitor PTSD symptoms, pain interference, sleep, and functioning at 4–6 week intervals.
Monitor cardiovascular risk factors (BP, lipids, weight) per standard guidelines.
reassessment_triggers: No meaningful PTSD or functional improvement after 6–8 weeks.
New or worsening safety concerns or adverse medication effects.
